compiled_state.description:
# Surface repeated non-fatal LLM step failures in gate run summaries

Split out of bug `tasty-unappeased-leopard` (b273-e0ba-f719-4f1c) at operator direction —
that report's fourth criterion. b273 (change 1624, merged) covers the build-drift warning
only; this ticket covers the invisibility of survived LLM step failures.

## Problem (premise confirmed in current code)

During a `review-plan` run, the overlap judge failed on EVERY batch:

    llm call [overlap-judge] mode=single_turn FAILED in 310.0s: Exceeded maximum output retries (2)
    overlap judge batch call failed; treating as abstain

Three batches, each ~310s, each ending in `abstain`. The failures are non-fatal by design,
so they never reach the verdict — the run paid ~15 minutes of wall time for a step that
contributed nothing and reported nothing a caller would notice.

Confirmed by reading the current tree:

- `src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py:203` swallows the batch failure to all-abstain, and
  `aggregate()` (`judge.py:226`) drops abstaining pairs entirely — so an `overlap[]` that
  is empty because every call died is **byte-identical** to one that is empty because
  nothing overlapped.
- There are ~13 such swallow sites across `src/rebar/llm/` (xcheck, completion_subcall,
  rising-floor novelty, ISF summarization, review_kernel novelty, code_review novelty,
  epic_bug_screen, overlap wire + judge). Each emits a `logger.warning` and nothing else.
- The plan-review verdict JSON has **no counter for survived failures**.
  `coverage.resolution_class` / `retryable` / `diagnostic` (`src/rebar/llm/failure.py:371`)
  fire only for a *fatal* systemic degrade. `coverage.chunk_errors`
  (`plan_review/pass1.py:590`) is the sole true counter and is write-only — no reader, no
  schema mention, no test — and it covers Pass-1 chunks only.
- Every failed LLM call already funnels through ONE seam —
  `PydanticAIRunner.run`'s except block at `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:573`, which already has
  the step's `_call_label` and already writes a spend row via `usage_log.record_failure`.
  That data goes to a JSONL spend log, never to the verdict.

So: repeated silent degradation is invisible to a caller consuming the gate's JSON.

## Design

Observability only. No new retry, no new control flow, no verdict change.

A run-scoped sink in a new leaf module `src/rebar/llm/step_failures.py`, mirroring the
established `review_kernel/telemetry.py` contract-violation sink verbatim: a
`contextvars.ContextVar` activated once per gate run, a `record` that is a no-op outside an
active scope, and a destructive `drain`. The module is a leaf — it imports only stdlib — so
the low `rebar.llm.runner` layer can record into it without the layering inversion
`build_drift.py` warns against (high pushes into low, never the reverse).

- **Record** at the single seam `runner.py:573`, beside the existing
  `usage_log.record_failure` call, keyed by the step's `_call_label`.
- **Activate** in the plan-review run scope in
  `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:155-166`, alongside `collect_contract_violations()`.
- **Drain** into `coverage` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:518-520`, using
  that site's exact posture: **present ONLY when non-empty**, so a clean run's verdict
  coverage stays byte-identical (attestation-safe) and the verdict string is untouched.

"Non-fatal" needs no classification at the record site: a fatal failure aborts the run and
returns a degraded verdict that never reaches the drain, so **every failure that appears in
a produced verdict is by construction one the run survived.**

Shape (`coverage.llm_step_failures`):

    {"total": 3, "by_step": {"overlap-judge": 3}}

## Scope / non-goals

- **Plan-review only.** `review-code` has a `coverage` object and `verify-completion` has
  none at all; extending either is deliberately out of scope and filed as a follow-up
  (`discovered_from` this ticket). The motivating incident is `review-plan`.
- Not changing any swallow site's behaviour — every abstain/degrade stays exactly as it is.
- Not adding retries, timeouts, or any verdict/exit-code effect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A `review-plan` run in which one or more LLM step calls fail but the run still
      produces a verdict carries `coverage.llm_step_failures` in the emitted JSON, shaped
      `{"total": <int>, "by_step": {<call label>: <int>}}`, where `total` is the number of
      failed LLM calls and `by_step` counts them per step label.
- [ ] AC2 — A run with NO failed LLM step calls does not carry the key at all: `coverage`
      is byte-identical to the pre-change output (attestation-safe, per the
      `verification_contract_violations` precedent).
- [ ] AC3 — The count never alters the `verdict` string, the exit code, the signature, or
      the provenance stamp; the failure classification and swallow behaviour of every
      existing site is unchanged.
- [ ] AC4 — The sink is run-scoped and does not leak: `record` outside an active scope is a
      no-op that never raises (so unit-testing a runner in isolation is unaffected), the
      scope is dropped on exit, and a second run in the same process starts from zero.
- [ ] AC5 — `coverage.llm_step_failures` is declared and described in
      `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json`, and the human-readable
      `review-plan` text output prints one line naming the total and the per-step counts
      when the key is present (and nothing when it is absent). The consumer that changes is
      **`_render_plan_review_text` in `src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:587`** — the renderer
      `_review_plan` (line 435) dispatches to at line 537. It reads `result["coverage"]`
      (which it already does for other keys) and is the ONLY renderer touched:
      `_render_review_text` (line 677, used by `_scan_spec` at line 337) and
      `_render_source_line` (line 65) are deliberately unchanged, consistent with the
      plan-review-only scope.
- [ ] AC6 — `by_step` keys use the runner's `_call_label` **verbatim**, so a key matches the
      `llm call [<label>] ... FAILED` log line an operator would grep. `_call_label`
      (`src/rebar/llm/runner.py:501-503`) is `",".join(req.reviewers)` when reviewers are
      present and otherwise falls back to the target ticket id (or the literal `"?"`); the
      schema description states this explicitly, including that unlabelled calls therefore
      group under that fallback key rather than under a step name.
- [ ] AC7 — Held-out unit tests cover: record→drain round-trip with multiple labels;
      no-failure run omits the key; record outside a scope is a silent no-op; drain is
      destructive so a second run starts at zero; and the verdict-assembly site adds the
      key only when non-empty.
- [ ] AC8 — One wiring test closes the gap between the unit tests and AC1's end-to-end
      claim: with the sink scope active, a runner call driven to failure (its provider
      stubbed to raise) is recorded under the expected label and reaches
      `coverage.llm_step_failures` through the same drain the verdict assembly uses — so the
      `runner.py` record site, the activated gate scope, and the drain are exercised
      together rather than only in isolation.
- [ ] AC9 — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the unit + interfaces suites pass; every
      touched file stays under the 800-LOC module cap (note `runner.py` is at 790 and
      `structured_run.py` at 796 — this is why the sink is a new leaf module rather than an
      addition to either).

## Notes

- Must remain non-fatal: this is reporting, not a new failure mode.
- Related: `7fa8102477` ("Bound malformed overlap judge calls") reduced the latency cost of
  the specific overlap-judge failure, but not the invisibility of the class.
